questions.stem: A conversion graph shows that $5$ miles is approximately $8$ km. Using this graph, approximately how many kilometres is $15$ miles?
questions.explanation: If $5$ miles $= 8$ km, then $1$ mile $= 1.6$ km. So $15$ miles $= 15 \times 1.6 = 24$ km.

questions.stem: On a speed-time graph, the area under the graph represents:
questions.explanation: The area under a speed-time graph gives the distance travelled. This is because distance $=$ speed $\times$ time.

questions.stem: A graph of temperature against time shows a steep section followed by a gentle section. This means the temperature:
questions.explanation: A steep positive gradient indicates a rapid increase, and a gentle positive gradient indicates a slower increase. So the temperature rose quickly at first, then more slowly.
